name: Banking
vision: Customers hold accounts, accounts move money, and every movement is a transfer that can fail halfway. The domain that has to get it right twice — once in the rules, once in the recovery.

aggregates.name: Customer
aggregates.description: A person the bank holds a relationship with. Suspended rather than deleted — a bank forgets nothing.

commands.name: Register
commands.goal: Take on a new customer

commands.name: Suspend
commands.goal: Stop a customer transacting while something is investigated

commands.name: Reinstate
commands.goal: Let a cleared customer transact again

commands.name: Close
commands.goal: End the relationship

queries.name: InGoodStanding
queries.description: The everyday customer roll — active, and nothing outstanding against them.

queries.name: Suspended
queries.description: The compliance queue, newest concern first.

queries.name: NotGoodStanding
queries.description: Everyone who is not in the everyday roll — suspended, under review, or anything else that is not simply "good".

aggregates.name: Account
aggregates.description: A balance belonging to one customer, and the ledger that explains how it got there.

invariants.description: a currency is a three-letter code
a currency is a three-letter code

commands.name: Open
commands.goal: Give a customer somewhere to keep money

commands.name: Credit
commands.goal: Put money in

commands.name: Debit
commands.goal: Take money out, if it is there to take

ensures.description: the balance fell by exactly the amount

commands.name: FreezeAccount
commands.goal: Stop an account moving while something is investigated

commands.name: Unfreeze
commands.goal: Release a cleared account

commands.name: CloseAccount
commands.goal: Close an account that has been emptied

commands.name: ApplyFee
commands.goal: Charge the account a fee

commands.name: CorrectFee
commands.goal: Reverse a fee that was applied in error

givens.description: a correction cannot exceed collected fees

fields.reason: "a fee was applied in error and is being reversed"

commands.name: AccrueInterest
commands.goal: Credit the account with interest earned

commands.name: CorrectInterest
commands.goal: Reverse interest that was accrued in error

givens.description: a correction cannot exceed accrued interest
the balance covers an interest correction

entities.name: LedgerEntry
entities.description: One movement across the account, in the order it was posted.

commands.name: Amend
commands.goal: Correct a movement posted for the wrong amount

givens.description: an amendment leaves a non-negative amount

commands.name: Reverse
commands.goal: Undo a movement that should not have been posted

queries.name: Reversed
queries.description: Entries that were undone — the audit trail nobody wants to need.

queries.name: Open
queries.description: Accounts that can transact today.

queries.name: Overdrawn
queries.description: Accounts below a floor the caller supplies — the morning risk report.

queries.name: HighBalance
queries.description: Accounts holding at least a floor the caller supplies — the private-banking referral list.

queries.name: StrictlyAbove
queries.description: Accounts holding MORE than a floor the caller supplies — the referral list without the accounts sitting exactly on the line.

queries.name: AtMost
queries.description: Accounts holding no more than a cap the caller supplies — the small-balance closure candidates.

queries.name: Reachable
queries.description: Accounts that still exist as far as a caller is concerned — anything short of closed.

queries.name: OpenForSuspendedCustomers
queries.description: Open accounts whose customer has since been suspended — live money movement nobody should be approving right now.

queries.name: OpenForCustomer
queries.description: One customer's own open accounts — the for_each target that freezes every one of them on suspension, not just whichever the event payload happened to carry.

aggregates.name: OnboardingCase
aggregates.description: The KYC check a newly registered customer clears before an account exists for them — screened once, and if it does not clear there is nothing to undo, because nothing was ever opened.

commands.name: Open
commands.goal: Open a KYC case for a newly registered customer, naming the account it will become

commands.name: Clear
commands.goal: Pass a customer's identity and screening checks

commands.name: Decline
commands.goal: Refuse a customer who does not clear screening — no account was ever opened, so nothing is undone

queries.name: Screening
queries.description: Cases still waiting on a compliance decision.

aggregates.name: ATMCard
aggregates.description: A card issued against an account, and the cash taken with it.

commands.name: Issue
commands.goal: Put a card in a customer's hand

commands.name: Rename
commands.goal: Name a card so it is recognisable

commands.name: Withdraw
commands.goal: Take cash out at a machine

commands.name: Activate
commands.goal: Start using a card

commands.name: Retire
commands.goal: Take a card out of service

entities.name: Withdrawal
entities.description: One handful of cash, in the order it was taken.

commands.name: Dispute
commands.goal: Challenge a withdrawal that was not mine

queries.name: Recent
queries.description: The first two withdrawals still standing, whatever else was taken.

queries.name: Active
queries.description: Live cards in nickname order, unnamed ones last — real nicknames sort among themselves first.

queries.name: ByFee
queries.description: Live cards by what they cost to hold, cheapest first — a fee is a Float, so the order is numeric and not alphabetical.

aggregates.name: CardPayment
aggregates.description: A card authorisation that either settles, is voided before settlement, or becomes a post-settlement dispute.

invariants.description: a tag is not the empty string

commands.name: Authorize
commands.goal: Put a hold on funds for a purchase

commands.name: Capture
commands.goal: Turn an authorization into an actual charge

commands.name: Void
commands.goal: Cancel an authorization before it settles

commands.name: Refund
commands.goal: Give the money back after a charge settled

commands.name: Reverse
commands.goal: Undo a captured charge with no customer dispute involved

commands.name: Dispute
commands.goal: Challenge a payment that already settled

commands.name: Chargeback
commands.goal: Uphold a customer's dispute and claw the charge back

commands.name: RejectDispute
commands.goal: Uphold the charge and close a customer's dispute

queries.name: Pending
queries.description: Authorized charges not yet captured, voided, or otherwise resolved.

queries.name: Disputed
queries.description: Charges currently under a customer's dispute, awaiting a compliance decision.

queries.name: Flagged
queries.description: Charges carrying a risk tag, for the fraud queue.

aggregates.name: SafeDepositBox
aggregates.description: A steel box in the vault, held under one customer's name and opened only against the branch and number stamped on its face.

invariants.description: a box is numbered from one

commands.name: Rent
commands.goal: Assign the box to a customer

commands.name: Surrender
commands.goal: Give the box back and take the keys off the account

commands.name: LogVisit
commands.goal: Record that the box was opened

commands.name: IssueKey
commands.goal: Cut a key for the box

entities.name: Visit
entities.description: One opening of the box, in the order it happened that day.

commands.name: Annotate
commands.goal: Note something unusual about a visit after the fact

queries.name: Recent
queries.description: The last few visits, whatever the box has seen.

invariants.description: a written note is not blank

entities.name: KeyIssuance
entities.description: One key cut for the box, held by whoever last signed for it.

commands.name: Return
commands.goal: Take a key back when a holder is done with it

queries.name: Rented
queries.description: Boxes currently assigned to a customer, for the annual access audit.

aggregates.name: Statement
aggregates.description: A snapshot of one account's activity over one period, generated once and never revised.

commands.name: Generate
commands.goal: Close out one period's activity into a permanent record

aggregates.name: Transfer
aggregates.description: Money leaving one account for another. Two movements that must both happen, or neither.

commands.name: Request
commands.goal: Send money to another account

commands.name: Debited
commands.goal: Record that the source account has given up the money

commands.name: Settle
commands.goal: Record that the destination has received it

commands.name: Credited
commands.goal: Record that the destination credit committed

commands.name: Reverse
commands.goal: Put the money back when the credit could not be made

commands.name: Reject
commands.goal: Refuse a transfer before any money moved

queries.name: InFlight
queries.description: Transfers that have left one account and not arrived at the other. The list that must always empty.

aggregates.name: ExternalTransfer
aggregates.description: A transfer sent beyond the bank, where a recall is an instruction and a return is the external network's outcome.

invariants.description: an external transfer amount is positive

commands.name: Request
commands.goal: Send money to an account outside the bank

commands.name: SendTransfer
commands.goal: Release the transfer to the external network

commands.name: Recall
commands.goal: Ask the external network to stop a transfer already sent

commands.name: Return
commands.goal: Record that the external network sent the money back

queries.name: Sent
queries.description: Transfers already released to the external network, awaiting its outcome.

aggregates.name: ScheduledPayment
aggregates.description: An instruction held for a future date, which may execute once or be cancelled before it does.

invariants.description: a scheduled payment amount is positive
a payment due date is present

commands.name: Schedule
commands.goal: Set up a payment to collect on a future date

commands.name: Execute
commands.goal: Collect a payment on its due date

commands.name: Cancel
commands.goal: Call off a payment before its due date

commands.name: Fail
commands.goal: Record that today's presentment could not be collected

commands.name: Retry
commands.goal: Re-present a failed payment, up to the limit the schedule names

ensures.description: a retry never lowers the attempt count

commands.name: Abandon
commands.goal: Give up on a payment that could not be collected after every retry

queries.name: Due
queries.description: Payments still scheduled, ordered by when they're due.

source_text:
Hecks.bluebook "Banking", version: "v1" do
  vision "Customers hold accounts, accounts move money, and every movement is a transfer that can fail halfway. The domain that has to get it right twice — once in the rules, once in the recovery."
  core
end

Hecks.bluebook "Banking" do
  read_model "CustomerPortfolio" do
    description "A customer's cross-account position, rebuilt from aggregate heads."
    reference_to Customer
    include Customer
    include Account
    include ATMCard
    include Transfer
    include CardPayment
    include ExternalTransfer
    include ScheduledPayment
  end

  # Rooted at an account, not a customer: holds and disputes are filed against accounts.
  read_model "ComplianceDashboard" do
    description "One account, its own status, and any card charges disputed against it — the working set for a compliance review."
    reference_to Account
    include Account
    include CardPayment

    # The one shape seal_query_options allows with several included aggregates: where/order_by/
    # limit apply to the single many-side collection (CardPayment).
    where(status: "disputed")
    order_by :amount, :desc
    limit 5
    # Second page: skip the first five, then take five (ADR 0025).
    offset 5
  end

  # Reductions rather than rows. `count`/`median` ride the same `where`; `seal_aggregation`
  # refuses combining either with `group_by` or with each other.
  read_model "DisputedPaymentCount" do
    description "How many of an account's own card charges are under dispute — a single number, not the rows themselves."
    reference_to Account
    include Account
    include CardPayment
    where(status: "disputed")
    count
  end

  read_model "DisputedPaymentMedian" do
    description "The median amount of an account's own disputed card charges."
    reference_to Account
    include Account
    include CardPayment
    where(status: "disputed")
    median :amount
  end

  # ADR 0078: sum/avg/min/max/percentile are siblings of count/median, same seal, same
  # `where(status: "disputed")` — the number a risk manager wants first (total exposure),
  # then its natural siblings (is that typical or one outlier, how bad is the worst one,
  # what does the tail look like).
  read_model "DisputedPaymentTotal" do
    description "The total amount of an account's own disputed card charges — the exposure a risk manager wants first."
    reference_to Account
    include Account
    include CardPayment
    where(status: "disputed")
    sum :amount
  end

  read_model "DisputedPaymentAverage" do
    description "The mean amount of an account's own disputed card charges — whether the total is one outlier or many similar ones."
    reference_to Account
    include Account
    include CardPayment
    where(status: "disputed")
    avg :amount
  end

  read_model "DisputedPaymentSmallest" do
    description "The smallest amount among an account's own disputed card charges."
    reference_to Account
    include Account
    include CardPayment
    where(status: "disputed")
    min :amount
  end

  read_model "DisputedPaymentLargest" do
    description "The largest amount among an account's own disputed card charges."
    reference_to Account
    include Account
    include CardPayment
    where(status: "disputed")
    max :amount
  end

  read_model "DisputedPaymentP95" do
    description "The 95th percentile amount of an account's own disputed card charges — the tail risk a median alone hides."
    reference_to Account
    include Account
    include CardPayment
    where(status: "disputed")
    percentile :amount, at: 0.95
  end

  # Rootless: no `reference_to` and no id at dispatch. Two `group_by` fields so the test
  # can tell real nesting from accidental flattening.
  read_model "AccountsByKind" do
    description "Every account the bank holds, sorted into what kind it is, then by its own number."
    include Account
    group_by :kind, :number
  end

end

Hecks.bluebook "Banking" do
  aggregate "Customer" do
    description "A person the bank holds a relationship with. Suspended rather than deleted — a bank forgets nothing."

    attribute :reference, CustomerNumber

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :name,      PersonName
    attribute :email,     EmailAddress
    attribute :standing,  CustomerStanding

    value_object "CustomerNumber" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a customer reference is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "CustomerStanding" do
      attribute :value, String, default: "good", pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a standing is named") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "PersonName" do
      attribute :given,  String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      attribute :family, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'

      invariant("a given name is present")  { !given.to_s.empty? }
      invariant("a family name is present") { !family.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "EmailAddress" do
      # The pattern uses explicit ranges rather than \S: perl classes differ between ASCII and
      # Unicode across regex engines, and PatternSubset refuses them.
      attribute :address, String, pattern: '^[^@ ]+@[^@ ]+\.[^@ ]+$'
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "active" do
      transition "Suspend"   => "suspended", from: "active"
      transition "Reinstate" => "active",    from: "suspended"
      transition "Close"     => "closed",    from: ["active", "suspended"]
    end

    command "Register" do
      role "Branch clerk"
      goal "Take on a new customer"

      sets :reference
      sets :name
      sets :email

      emits CustomerRegistered
    end

    # `from:` gates the command on lifecycle state; the refusal wording matches the
    # lifecycle transition's own (ADR 0025).
    command "Suspend", from: "active" do
      role "Compliance officer"
      goal "Stop a customer transacting while something is investigated"

      reference_to Customer

      sets :standing

      emits CustomerSuspended
    end

    command "Reinstate", from: "suspended" do
      role "Compliance officer"
      goal "Let a cleared customer transact again"

      reference_to Customer
      sets :standing, to: { value: "good" }

      emits CustomerReinstated
    end

    command "Close", from: ["active", "suspended"] do
      role "Branch clerk"
      goal "End the relationship"

      reference_to Customer
      emits CustomerClosed
    end

    query "InGoodStanding" do
      description "The everyday customer roll — active, and nothing outstanding against them."
      where(status: "active", standing: "good")
      order_by :reference
    end

    query "Suspended" do
      description "The compliance queue, newest concern first."
      where(status: "suspended")
      order_by :reference, :desc
      limit 50
    end

    query "NotGoodStanding" do
      description "Everyone who is not in the everyday roll — suspended, under review, or anything else that is not simply \"good\"."
      where(standing: { ne: "good" })
      order_by :reference
    end
  end

end

Hecks.bluebook "Banking" do
  aggregate "Account" do
    description "A balance belonging to one customer, and the ledger that explains how it got there."
    provenance from: { source: "HecksCanonical", source_id: "aggregate:account", source_version: "1.0" }

    reference_to Customer

    attribute :number, AccountNumber

    identified_by :number

    attribute :balance,      Money
    attribute :kind,         AccountKind
    attribute :daily_limit,  DailyLimit
    attribute :ledger,       list_of(LedgerEntry)
    attribute :fees_cents,   Money
    attribute :interest_cents, Money

    value_object "AccountNumber" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("an account number is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "DailyLimit" do
      attribute :cents, Integer, default: 0
      invariant("a daily limit is non-negative") { !cents.negative? }
    end

    value_object "LedgerSequence" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("a ledger sequence is positive") { value.positive? }
    end

    value_object "LedgerDirection" do
      attribute :value, String, one_of: ["credit", "debit"]
    end

    value_object "Money" do
      attribute :cents,    Integer, default: 0
      attribute :currency, String,  default: "USD"

      invariant("a currency is a three-letter code") { currency.to_s.size == 3 }
    end

    value_object "PositiveMoney" do
      attribute :cents,    Integer
      attribute :currency, String, default: "USD"

      invariant("an amount is positive") { cents.positive? }
      invariant("a currency is a three-letter code")
    end

    value_object "AccountKind" do
      attribute :name, String, one_of: ["current", "savings", "reserve"]
    end

    value_object "Narrative" do
      attribute :text, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'

      invariant("a movement explains itself") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    entity "LedgerEntry" do
      given("entry is posted") { state == "posted" }
      description "One movement across the account, in the order it was posted."

      attribute :sequence, LedgerSequence

      identified_by :sequence

      attribute :amount,    Money
      attribute :narrative, Narrative
      attribute :direction, LedgerDirection

      # Shared by Amend and Reverse, and bare-referenced by SafeDepositBox::Visit as
      # `declared_by: "Account.LedgerEntry"` (ADR 0028).
      # `parent.customer_status`, not `parent.customer.status`: a rule may read only its own
      # aggregate's fields, and `customer_status` is projected into Account (ADR 0025).
      given("customer is active") { parent.customer_status == "active" }
      given("account is open")    { parent.status == "open" }

      lifecycle :state, default: "posted" do
        transition "Reverse" => "reversed", from: "posted"
        transition "Amend"   => "posted",   from: "posted"
      end

      command "Amend" do
        role "Back office"
        goal "Correct a movement posted for the wrong amount"

        attribute :adjustment, Money
        given("customer is active")
        given("account is open")
        given("entry is posted")

        given("an amendment leaves a non-negative amount") { amount.cents + adjustment.cents >= 0 }

        sets :amount,    increment: :adjustment
        sets :narrative

        emits LedgerEntryAmended
      end

      command "Reverse" do
        role "Back office"
        goal "Undo a movement that should not have been posted"

        given("customer is active")
        given("account is open")
        given("entry is posted")
        sets :narrative

        emits LedgerEntryReversed
      end

      query "Reversed" do
        description "Entries that were undone — the audit trail nobody wants to need."
        where(state: "reversed")
      end
    end

    # Checked after every command, before save, so every command that moves :balance is covered
    # (ADR 0025).
    invariant("the balance never goes negative") { balance.cents >= 0 }

    # A held copy of Customer's status, refreshed by a rebuild sweep (runtime/rebuild_sweep.rb).
    # Rules may read only their own aggregate boundary, so a customer suspended a moment ago can
    # still pass "customer is active" until the next sweep.
    projects :customer_status, from: :"customer.status"

    # Shared by every acting command on Account. `Open` does not reference it: it creates the
    # record, so `customer` there is a command argument, not stored state. FreezeAccount and
    # CloseAccount use "customer is not closed" instead. LedgerEntry reads
    # `parent.customer_status`, a different path, so it keeps its own given.
    given("customer is active") { customer_status == "active" }

    # Shared by the two compliance-adjacent commands, FreezeAccount and CloseAccount.
    given("customer is not closed") { customer_status != "closed" }

    lifecycle :status, default: "open" do
      transition "FreezeAccount" => "frozen", from: "open"
      transition "Unfreeze" => "open",  from: "frozen"
      transition "CloseAccount" => "closed", from: ["open", "frozen"]
    end

    command "Open" do
      role "Branch clerk"
      goal "Give a customer somewhere to keep money"

      # Not the shared given: `customer` here is a fresh command argument, resolved
      # synchronously, and `customer_status` does not exist until this command creates the record.
      given("customer is active") { customer.status == "active" }

      sets :customer
      sets :number
      sets :kind
      sets :daily_limit

      emits AccountOpened
    end

    # `from:` names the legal lifecycle state, so it is checkable against the state machine.
    command "Credit", from: "open" do
      role "Teller"
      goal "Put money in"

      reference_to Account
      attribute :amount,    PositiveMoney

      given("customer is active")
      sets :balance, increment: :amount
      sets :ledger,  append: { amount: :amount, narrative: :narrative, direction: { value: "credit" } }

      emits AccountCredited
    end

    command "Debit", from: "open" do
      role "Teller"
      goal "Take money out, if it is there to take"

      reference_to Account
      attribute :amount,    PositiveMoney

      given("customer is active")
      given("the balance covers it")     { balance.cents >= amount.cents }
      given("the daily limit allows it") { daily_limit.cents >= amount.cents }

      sets :balance, decrement: :amount
      sets :ledger,  append: { amount: :amount, narrative: :narrative, direction: { value: "debit" } }

      # The aggregate invariant above covers "the balance never goes negative".
      ensures("the balance fell by exactly the amount") { old.balance.cents == balance.cents + amount.cents }
      ensures("a ledger entry was posted") { ledger.size == old.ledger.size + 1 }

      emits AccountDebited
    end

    command "FreezeAccount", from: "open" do
      role "Compliance officer"
      goal "Stop an account moving while something is investigated"

      reference_to Account
      # "customer is not closed", not "customer is active": FreezeAccountsOnSuspension fires
      # because a customer was just suspended, so an active-only guard could never pass.
      # No `standing` attribute is needed: the policy projects with `with: { account: :account }`.
      given("customer is not closed")
      # Bare event constant, matched by ReviewOnFreeze's `on Account::AccountFrozen`.
      emits AccountFrozen
    end

    command "Unfreeze", from: "frozen" do
      role "Compliance officer"
      goal "Release a cleared account"

      reference_to Account
      given("customer is active")
      emits AccountUnfrozen
    end

    command "CloseAccount", from: ["open", "frozen"] do
      role "Branch clerk"
      goal "Close an account that has been emptied"

      reference_to Account
      given("customer is not closed")

      given("an account closes empty") { balance.cents.zero? }

      emits AccountClosed
    end

    command "ApplyFee", from: "open" do
      role "System"
      goal "Charge the account a fee"

      reference_to Account
      attribute :amount, PositiveMoney
      attribute :narrative, Narrative
      given("customer is active")
      given("the balance covers a fee") { balance.cents >= amount.cents }
      sets :balance, decrement: :amount
      sets :fees_cents, increment: :amount
      emits FeeApplied
    end

    command "CorrectFee", from: "open" do
      role "Back office"
      goal "Reverse a fee that was applied in error"

      reference_to Account
      attribute :amount, PositiveMoney
      # `corrects` checks that a fee was actually applied (`NothingToCorrect`).
      corrects "FeeApplied", reason: "a fee was applied in error and is being reversed"
      given("customer is active")
      given("a correction cannot exceed collected fees") { fees_cents.cents >= amount.cents }
      sets :balance, increment: :amount
      sets :fees_cents, decrement: :amount
      emits FeeCorrected
    end

    command "AccrueInterest", from: "open" do
      role "System"
      goal "Credit the account with interest earned"

      reference_to Account
      attribute :amount, PositiveMoney
      given("customer is active")
      sets :balance, increment: :amount
      sets :interest_cents, increment: :amount
      emits InterestAccrued
    end

    command "CorrectInterest", from: "open" do
      role "Back office"
      goal "Reverse interest that was accrued in error"

      reference_to Account
      attribute :amount, PositiveMoney
      given("customer is active")
      given("a correction cannot exceed accrued interest") { interest_cents.cents >= amount.cents }
      given("the balance covers an interest correction") { balance.cents >= amount.cents }
      sets :balance, decrement: :amount
      sets :interest_cents, decrement: :amount
      emits InterestCorrected
    end

    query "Open" do
      description "Accounts that can transact today."
      where(status: "open")
      order_by :number
    end

    query "Overdrawn" do
      description "Accounts below a floor the caller supplies — the morning risk report."
      attribute :floor, Money
      where(balance: { lt: :floor })
      order_by :balance
      limit 100
    end

    query "HighBalance" do
      description "Accounts holding at least a floor the caller supplies — the private-banking referral list."
      attribute :floor, Money
      where(balance: { gte: :floor })
      order_by :balance, :desc
    end

    query "StrictlyAbove" do
      description "Accounts holding MORE than a floor the caller supplies — the referral list without the accounts sitting exactly on the line."
      attribute :floor, Money
      where(balance: { gt: :floor })
      order_by :balance, :desc
    end

    query "AtMost" do
      description "Accounts holding no more than a cap the caller supplies — the small-balance closure candidates."
      attribute :cap, Money
      where(balance: { lte: :cap })
      order_by :balance
    end

    query "Reachable" do
      description "Accounts that still exist as far as a caller is concerned — anything short of closed."
      where(status: { in: "open,frozen" })
      order_by :number
    end

    # Dotted where: `customer/status` hops through the reference and checks the target's field.
    query "OpenForSuspendedCustomers" do
      description "Open accounts whose customer has since been suspended — live money movement nobody should be approving right now."
      where(status: "open")
      where(:"customer/status" => "suspended")
      order_by :number
    end

    # The for_each target for FreezeAccountsOnSuspension. Scoped to one customer, unlike the
    # dashboard query above, so a suspension does not refire other customers' accounts.
    # `reference` is the key CustomerSuspended's payload carries, not a `customer_id` foreign key.
    query "OpenForCustomer" do
      description "One customer's own open accounts — the for_each target that freezes every one of them on suspension, not just whichever the event payload happened to carry."
      # Plain String, not Customer's CustomerNumber: query attribute types are never coerced
      # (`QueryInterpreter#resolve_query_value`), and a VO from another aggregate cannot be fuzzed.
      attribute :reference, String
      where(customer: :reference, status: "open")
      order_by :number
    end

    policy "ReviewOnFreeze" do
      # Bare event constant, matching FreezeAccount's `emits AccountFrozen`.
      on      Account::AccountFrozen
      trigger AccountFreezeReview::Open
      across  "Compliance"
    end
  end

  # One suspension freezes every open account the customer holds.
  #
  # `for_each_key` is resolved at codegen through `Behaviour::Command#addressing_key_for`,
  # never re-derived in the kernel: `account` for a self-referencing command, `account_id`
  # for one merely holding a reference. `with:` sends only the row, so FreezeAccount need not
  # declare a `standing` it never reads.
  #
  # The parser does not yet build `where` on a policy (it is a block, not a positional text).
  policy "FreezeAccountsOnSuspension" do
    on       Customer::CustomerSuspended
    for_each "Account.OpenForCustomer"
    # `account` is the key the fan-out merges per row; naming it keeps `standing` off the payload.
    trigger  Account::FreezeAccount, with: { account: :account }
  end

  # Notifications does not exist on purpose: this exercises the undelivered-reaction path
  # (spec/runtime/policy_spec.rb). ModelCheck holds the expectation and fails if it goes stale.
  policy "NotifyOnClosure" do
    on      Account::AccountClosed
    trigger Notifications::Send
    across  "Notifications", expect_undelivered: true
  end

end

Hecks.bluebook "Banking" do
  aggregate "OnboardingCase" do
    given("case is screening") { status == "screening" }
    # Shared given; see SafeDepositBox for why `declared_by:` is required.
    given("customer is active", declared_by: Account)
    description "The KYC check a newly registered customer clears before an account exists for them — screened once, and if it does not clear there is nothing to undo, because nothing was ever opened."

    # Mints a bare `customer` attribute, no `_id` suffix (ADR 0025).
    reference_to Customer
    # Must match Account's projected field name: the shared given reads `customer_status`.
    projects :customer_status, from: :"customer.status"

    attribute :reference, OnboardingReference

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :account_number, AccountNumber

    value_object "OnboardingReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("an onboarding case is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "AccountNumber" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("an account number is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "screening" do
      transition "Clear"   => "cleared",  from: "screening"
      transition "Decline" => "declined", from: "screening"
    end

    command "Open" do
      role "Branch clerk"
      goal "Open a KYC case for a newly registered customer, naming the account it will become"

      # Own given: `customer` is a fresh command argument, not yet stored state.
      given("customer is active") { customer.status == "active" }

      sets :customer
      sets :reference
      sets :account_number

      emits OnboardingOpened
    end

    command "Clear", from: "screening" do
      role "Compliance officer"
      goal "Pass a customer's identity and screening checks"

      reference_to OnboardingCase
      given("customer is active")

      emits OnboardingCleared
    end

    command "Decline", from: "screening" do
      role "Compliance officer"
      goal "Refuse a customer who does not clear screening — no account was ever opened, so nothing is undone"

      reference_to OnboardingCase
      given("customer is active")

      emits OnboardingDeclined
    end

    query "Screening" do
      description "Cases still waiting on a compliance decision."
      where(status: "screening")
      order_by :reference
    end
  end

  # A saga with no compensating leg: a declined KYC case opened no account
  # and moved no money, so there is nothing to undo.
  process_manager "Onboarding" do
    correlates_by :"reference.value"
    starts_on OnboardingCase::OnboardingOpened
    ends_on   Account::AccountOpened

    transition OnboardingCase::OnboardingCleared => "cleared", from: "screening" do
      # Kind and limit are the bank's default terms; later changes go through Account.
      dispatch Account::Open, with: {
        customer:    :customer,
        number:      :account_number,
        kind:        { name: "current" },
        daily_limit: { cents: 0 }
      }
    end

    # No dispatch: nothing was created to undo.
    transition OnboardingCase::OnboardingDeclined => "declined", from: "screening"
  end
end

Hecks.bluebook "Banking" do
  aggregate "ATMCard" do
    given("card is issued or active") { ["issued", "active"].include?(status) }
    # Acting commands read projected fields, not dot-paths (ADR 0025); `Issue`
    # keeps dot-paths because `account` is a fresh argument there, not stored state.
    given("account is open") { account_status == "open" }
    given("customer is active") { account_customer_status == "active" }
    description "A card issued against an account, and the cash taken with it."

    reference_to Account
    projects :account_status,          from: :"account.status"
    projects :account_customer_status, from: :"account.customer_status"

    attribute :serial, CardSerial

    identified_by :serial

    # Optional: a card handed over the same day often has no nickname yet, and
    # the `Active` query's `nulls` ordering relies on true absence.
    attribute :nickname,    CardNickname, optional: true
    attribute :daily_fee,   DailyFee
    attribute :withdrawals, list_of(Withdrawal)

    value_object "CardSerial" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a card serial is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "CardNickname" do
      attribute :value, String
    end

    value_object "DailyFee" do
      attribute :amount, Float, default: 0.0
      invariant("a daily fee is non-negative") { amount >= 0 }
    end

    value_object "WithdrawalSequence" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("a withdrawal sequence is positive") { value.positive? }
    end

    value_object "WithdrawalAmount" do
      attribute :cents, Integer
      invariant("a withdrawal amount is positive") { cents.positive? }
    end

    value_object "Narrative" do
      attribute :text, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'

      invariant("a withdrawal explains itself") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    entity "Withdrawal" do
      description "One handful of cash, in the order it was taken."

      attribute :sequence, WithdrawalSequence

      identified_by :sequence

      attribute :cents,     WithdrawalAmount
      attribute :narrative, Narrative

      lifecycle :state, default: "taken" do
        transition "Dispute" => "disputed", from: "taken"
      end

      command "Dispute", from: "taken" do
        role "Customer"
        goal "Challenge a withdrawal that was not mine"

        # Reads ATMCard's projected fields, already part of `parent.state` (ADR 0025).
        given("customer is active") { parent.account_customer_status == "active" }
        given("account is open") { parent.account_status == "open" }
        # Must read `parent.status`: Withdrawal's own lifecycle field is `:state`,
        # so a bare `status` would never refuse disputes on a retired card.
        given("card is not retired") { parent.status != "retired" }
        sets :narrative

        emits WithdrawalDisputed
      end

      query "Recent" do
        description "The first two withdrawals still standing, whatever else was taken."
        where(state: "taken")
        limit 2
      end
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "issued" do
      transition "Activate" => "active",  from: "issued"
      transition "Retire"   => "retired", from: ["issued", "active"]
    end

    command "Issue" do
      role "Branch clerk"
      goal "Put a card in a customer's hand"

      # Own givens: `account` is a fresh command argument, while the projected
      # fields the shared givens read are not stored until this command runs.
      given("customer is active") { account.customer.status == "active" }
      given("account is open") { account.status == "open" }

      sets :account
      sets :serial
      sets :daily_fee

      emits ATMCardIssued
    end

    # `Rename`/`Withdraw` have no matching transition, so `from:` is their only
    # state guard. `Activate`/`Retire` repeat their transition's check so the
    # command signature states the state it needs.
    command "Rename", from: ["issued", "active"] do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Name a card so it is recognisable"

      reference_to ATMCard
      attribute :nickname, CardNickname
      given("customer is active")
      sets :nickname

      emits ATMCardRenamed
    end

    command "Withdraw", from: "active" do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Take cash out at a machine"

      reference_to ATMCard
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      # Narrower than Rename/Retire on purpose: an issued card must be activated first.

      sets :withdrawals, append: { cents: :cents, narrative: :narrative }

      emits CashWithdrawn
    end

    command "Activate", from: "issued" do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Start using a card"

      reference_to ATMCard
      given("customer is active")
      emits ATMCardActivated
    end

    command "Retire", from: ["issued", "active"] do
      role "Back office"
      goal "Take a card out of service"

      reference_to ATMCard
      given("customer is active")
      emits ATMCardRetired
    end

    # `nulls :last` puts unnamed cards after every named one, explicitly.
    query "Active" do
      description "Live cards in nickname order, unnamed ones last — real nicknames sort among themselves first."
      where(status: "active")
      order_by :nickname
      nulls :last
    end

    # `offset 1` skips the cheapest card, then `limit 3` takes the next three.
    query "ByFee" do
      description "Live cards by what they cost to hold, cheapest first — a fee is a Float, so the order is numeric and not alphabetical."
      where(status: "active")
      order_by :daily_fee
      limit 3
      offset 1
    end
  end

  aggregate "CardPayment" do
    given("payment is disputed") { status == "disputed" }
    given("payment is captured") { status == "captured" }
    given("payment is authorized") { status == "authorized" }
    # Shared with ATMCard; `declared_by:` is required because Account's
    # "customer is active" is a different canonical.
    given("account is open", declared_by: ATMCard)
    given("customer is active", declared_by: ATMCard)
    description "A card authorisation that either settles, is voided before settlement, or becomes a post-settlement dispute."

    reference_to Account
    # Same names as ATMCard's projected fields: the shared givens read them by name.
    projects :account_status,          from: :"account.status"
    projects :account_customer_status, from: :"account.customer_status"
    # Optional: nil until `Dispute` sets it, and an undisputed payment must still save.
    reference_to Customer, as: :disputed_by, optional: true
    attribute :authorisation, AuthorisationCode

    identified_by :authorisation
    attribute :amount,   PaymentAmount

    value_object "AuthorisationCode" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
    end
    attribute :merchant, MerchantName

    value_object "PaymentAmount" do
      attribute :cents, Integer
      invariant("a payment amount is positive") { cents.positive? }
    end

    value_object "MerchantName" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a merchant name is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # Free-form risk tags, not a closed set: the risk desk adds tags before the model names them.
    attribute :tags, list_of(Tag)

    value_object "Tag" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a tag is not the empty string") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "authorized" do
      transition "Capture" => "captured", from: "authorized"
      transition "Void" => "voided", from: "authorized"
      transition "Refund" => "refunded", from: "captured"
      transition "Reverse" => "reversed", from: "captured"
      transition "Dispute" => "disputed", from: ["captured", "refunded"]
      transition "Chargeback" => "charged_back", from: "disputed"
      transition "RejectDispute" => "captured", from: "disputed"
    end

    command "Authorize" do
      # Role-less on purpose: diagrams_spec and oidc_projection_spec depend on
      # Banking having one unguarded command, and this is it.
      goal "Put a hold on funds for a purchase"
      attribute :authorisation, AuthorisationCode
      attribute :tags, list_of(Tag), optional: true
      # Own givens: `account` is a fresh command argument; see ATMCard.Issue.
      given("customer is active") { account.customer.status == "active" }
      given("account is open") { account.status == "open" }
      sets :account
      sets :amount
      sets :merchant
      sets :tags
      sets :authorisation
      emits CardAuthorized
    end

    command "Capture", from: "authorized" do
      role "System"
      goal "Turn an authorization into an actual charge"

      reference_to CardPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits CardCaptured
    end

    command "Void", from: "authorized" do
      role "System"
      goal "Cancel an authorization before it settles"

      reference_to CardPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits CardVoided
    end

    command "Refund", from: "captured" do
      role "System"
      goal "Give the money back after a charge settled"

      reference_to CardPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits CardRefunded
    end

    command "Reverse", from: "captured" do
      role "System"
      goal "Undo a captured charge with no customer dispute involved"

      reference_to CardPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits CardReversed
    end

    command "Dispute", from: ["captured", "refunded"] do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Challenge a payment that already settled"

      # Carries both a self reference and a cross-aggregate one: on a joint account
      # the disputant is not derivable from the payment. The owner match keeps
      # Dispute non-creating; Customer becomes a Reference attribute.
      reference_to CardPayment
      reference_to Customer, as: :disputed_by
      given("account is open")
      given("customer is active") { disputed_by.status == "active" }

      sets :disputed_by

      emits CardDisputed
    end

    command "Chargeback", from: "disputed" do
      role "Compliance officer"
      goal "Uphold a customer's dispute and claw the charge back"

      reference_to CardPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits CardChargedBack
    end

    command "RejectDispute", from: "disputed" do
      role "Compliance officer"
      goal "Uphold the charge and close a customer's dispute"

      reference_to CardPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits CardDisputeRejected
    end

    query "Pending" do
      description "Authorized charges not yet captured, voided, or otherwise resolved."
      where(status: "authorized")
    end

    query "Disputed" do
      description "Charges currently under a customer's dispute, awaiting a compliance decision."
      where(status: "disputed")
    end

    query "Flagged" do
      description "Charges carrying a risk tag, for the fraud queue."
      where(tags: { contains: "high_risk" })
    end
  end

end

Hecks.bluebook "Banking" do
  aggregate "SafeDepositBox" do
    # Shared with Account (deposit_accounts.bluebook): both hold a direct
    # `reference_to Customer`. `declared_by:` disambiguates ATMCard's different given.
    given("customer is active", declared_by: Account)
    description "A steel box in the vault, held under one customer's name and opened only against the branch and number stamped on its face."

    belongs_to Customer

    # Same local copy Account declares; each aggregate projects independently (ADR 0025).
    projects :customer_status, from: :"customer.status"

    # Box numbers repeat across branches, so identity is composite: branch and number.
    attribute :branch_code, BranchCode
    attribute :box_number,  BoxNumber

    identified_by :branch_code, :box_number
    # Inline `one_of` as an attribute type synthesises the "Size" value object.
    attribute :size,   one_of("small", "medium", "large"), default: { value: "small" }
    attribute :visits, list_of(Visit)
    attribute :keys,   list_of(KeyIssuance)

    value_object "BranchCode" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a branch is coded") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "BoxNumber" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("a box is numbered from one") { value.positive? }
    end

    value_object "VisitSequence" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("a visit sequence is positive") { value.positive? }
    end

    value_object "VisitDate" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a visit names its date") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "VisitNote" do
      attribute :text, String
    end

    value_object "KeySerial" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a key is serialed") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # Composite identity under a composite head: a box may open twice in one day.
    entity "Visit" do
      description "One opening of the box, in the order it happened that day."

      attribute :date,     VisitDate
      attribute :sequence, VisitSequence

      identified_by :date, :sequence
      # Optional: most openings are routine.
      attribute :note,     VisitNote, optional: true

      # Lives here, not on VisitNote: a value object invariant never runs for an
      # absent optional field, so only the owner can tell absent from empty.
      invariant("a written note is not blank") { !note || !note.text.to_s.empty? }

      # Shared with Account::LedgerEntry: both read `parent.customer_status` (ADR 0025).
      # Cannot reuse the aggregate-level given, whose path is `customer_status`,
      # not `parent.customer_status`.
      given("customer is active")
      given("box is rented") { parent.status == "rented" }

      lifecycle :state, default: "logged" do
        transition "Annotate" => "logged", from: "logged"
      end

      command "Annotate", from: "logged" do
        role "Vault officer"
        goal "Note something unusual about a visit after the fact"

        attribute :note,     VisitNote
        given("customer is active")
        given("box is rented")

        sets :note

        emits VisitAnnotated
      end

      query "Recent" do
        description "The last few visits, whatever the box has seen."
        where(state: "logged")
        limit 5
      end
    end

    # Identified by a single field where Visit uses two, so runtimes must pick the named entity.
    entity "KeyIssuance" do
      description "One key cut for the box, held by whoever last signed for it."

      attribute :serial, KeySerial

      identified_by :serial

      lifecycle :status, default: "issued" do
        transition "Return" => "returned", from: "issued"
      end

      command "Return" do
        role "Vault officer"
        goal "Take a key back when a holder is done with it"

        attribute :serial, KeySerial
        # Shared with Visit through the aggregate's cross-entity given pool.
        given("customer is active")
        given("box is rented")

        emits KeyReturned
      end
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "vacant" do
      transition "Rent"      => "rented", from: "vacant"
      transition "Surrender" => "vacant", from: "rented"
    end

    # `LogVisit`/`IssueKey` have no matching transition, so `from:` is their only state guard.
    command "Rent", from: "vacant" do
      role "Branch clerk"
      goal "Assign the box to a customer"

      attribute :branch_code, BranchCode
      attribute :box_number,  BoxNumber
      attribute :size,        Size
      # Own given: `customer` is a fresh argument and `customer_status` is not
      # seeded until the box is saved; see Account.Open.
      given("customer is active") { customer.status == "active" }

      sets :customer
      sets :branch_code
      sets :box_number
      sets :size

      emits BoxRented
    end

    command "Surrender", from: "rented" do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Give the box back and take the keys off the account"

      reference_to SafeDepositBox

      given("customer is active")

      # Two facts from one act: the surrender, and the keys still outstanding.
      emits BoxSurrendered
      emits KeyReturnDue
    end

    command "LogVisit", from: "rented" do
      role "Vault officer"
      goal "Record that the box was opened"

      reference_to SafeDepositBox

      given("customer is active")

      sets :visits, append: { date: :date, sequence: :sequence, note: :note }

      emits BoxOpened
    end

    command "IssueKey", from: "rented" do
      role "Vault officer"
      goal "Cut a key for the box"

      reference_to SafeDepositBox
      given("customer is active")

      sets :keys, append: { serial: :serial }

      emits KeyIssued
    end

    query "Rented" do
      description "Boxes currently assigned to a customer, for the annual access audit."
      where(status: "rented")
      order_by :branch_code
      # Vault records are read only against the caller's own branch.
      authorize :vault_access, tenant: :branch_code
    end
  end

  # One policy per fact Surrender announces.
  policy "ReviewOnBoxSurrender" do
    on      SafeDepositBox::BoxSurrendered
    trigger BoxSurrenderReview::Open
    across  "Compliance"
  end

  policy "FlagKeyReturn" do
    on      SafeDepositBox::KeyReturnDue
    trigger Notifications::Send
    # Undelivered on purpose; see NotifyOnClosure in deposit_accounts.bluebook.
    across  "Notifications", expect_undelivered: true
  end

end

Hecks.bluebook "Banking" do
  aggregate "Statement" do
    description "A snapshot of one account's activity over one period, generated once and never revised."

    reference_to Account
    attribute :period,          StatementPeriod
    attribute :opening_balance, StatementAmount
    attribute :closing_balance, StatementAmount
    attribute :generated_on,    StatementDate
    attribute :frequency,       StatementFrequency

    # Composite identity whose first part is a reference: `account` is already a
    # scalar id (ADR 0025), so there is no value object to unwrap.
    identified_by :account, :period

    value_object "StatementPeriod" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a statement names its period") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

      attribute :cents, Integer
    end

    value_object "StatementDate" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a statement is dated") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # A closed set with several fields per member, so `one_of:` does not fit.

    value_object "StatementFrequency" do
      attribute :cadence,          String
      attribute :retention_months, Integer
      attribute :paper_fee_cents,  Integer

      member cadence: "monthly",   retention_months: 84,  paper_fee_cents: 0
      member cadence: "quarterly", retention_months: 120, paper_fee_cents: 0
      member cadence: "annual",    retention_months: 240, paper_fee_cents: 500
    end

    command "Generate" do
      role "System"
      goal "Close out one period's activity into a permanent record"

      attribute :period,          StatementPeriod
      attribute :opening_balance, StatementAmount
      attribute :closing_balance, StatementAmount
      attribute :generated_on,    StatementDate
      attribute :frequency,       StatementFrequency
      # Own givens: `account` is a fresh command argument, and nothing here populates
      # the projected field that ATMCard's shared givens read.
      given("customer is active") { account.customer.status == "active" }
      given("account is open") { account.status == "open" }

      sets :account
      # Bare `sets` imports the matching attribute; omitting one leaves it nil on the record.
      sets :period
      sets :opening_balance
      sets :closing_balance
      sets :generated_on
      sets :frequency

      emits StatementGenerated
    end
  end

Hecks.bluebook "Banking" do
  aggregate "Transfer" do
    given("transfer is debited") { status == "debited" }
    # Shared givens for the acting commands read projected fields; `Request` keeps dot-path copies
    # because its `source`/`destination` are fresh arguments, not stored state.
    given("destination account is open") { destination_account_status == "open" }
    given("destination customer is active") { destination_customer_status == "active" }
    given("transfer is requested") { status == "requested" }
    given("source account is open") { source_account_status == "open" }
    given("source customer is active") { source_customer_status == "active" }
    description "Money leaving one account for another. Two movements that must both happen, or neither."

    reference_to Account, as: :source
    reference_to Account, as: :destination

    # `source` and `destination` both reference Account; each projects its own copies, read through
    # the local reference name rather than the target type.
    projects :source_account_status,       from: :"source.status"
    projects :source_customer_status,      from: :"source.customer_status"
    projects :destination_account_status,  from: :"destination.status"
    projects :destination_customer_status, from: :"destination.customer_status"

    attribute :reference, TransferReference

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :amount,    TransferMoney

    value_object "TransferReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a transfer is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end
    attribute :narrative, Narrative

    value_object "TransferMoney" do
      attribute :cents, Integer
      invariant("a transfer amount is positive") { cents.positive? }
    end

    value_object "Narrative" do
      attribute :text, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'

      invariant("a transfer explains itself") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "requested" do
      transition "Debited"  => "debited",   from: "requested"
      transition "Credited" => "credited",  from: "debited"
      transition "Settle"   => "settled",   from: "credited"
      transition "Reverse"  => "reversed",  from: "debited"
      transition "Reject"   => "rejected",  from: "requested"
    end

    command "Request" do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Send money to another account"

      attribute :reference,   TransferReference

      # Fresh command arguments, so these read the dot-path directly; the shared givens above read
      # projected fields that exist only after this command creates the record.
      given("source customer is active") { source.customer.status == "active" }
      given("source account is open") { source.status == "open" }
      # `.empty?`, not `.to_s.empty?`: a valid reference dereferences to a Hash,
      # which `.to_s` cannot render.
      given("a transfer names its source")  { !source.empty? }
      given("a transfer goes somewhere")    { !destination.empty? }
      given("a transfer moves BETWEEN accounts") { source != destination }

      sets :amount
      sets :narrative
      sets :source
      sets :destination
      sets :reference

      emits TransferRequested
    end

    # Each `from:` below matches a `transition` above.
    command "Debited", from: "requested" do
      role "System"
      goal "Record that the source account has given up the money"

      reference_to Transfer
      given("source customer is active")
      given("source account is open")
      emits TransferDebited
    end

    command "Settle", from: "credited" do
      role "System"
      goal "Record that the destination has received it"

      reference_to Transfer
      given("destination customer is active")
      given("destination account is open")
      emits TransferSettled
    end

    command "Credited", from: "debited" do
      role "System"
      goal "Record that the destination credit committed"

      reference_to Transfer
      given("destination customer is active")
      given("destination account is open")
      emits TransferCredited
    end

    command "Reverse", from: "debited" do
      role "System"
      goal "Put the money back when the credit could not be made"

      reference_to Transfer
      given("source customer is active")
      given("source account is open")
      emits TransferReversed
    end

    command "Reject", from: "requested" do
      role "System"
      goal "Refuse a transfer before any money moved"

      reference_to Transfer
      given("source customer is active")
      given("source account is open")
      emits TransferRejected
    end

    query "InFlight" do
      description "Transfers that have left one account and not arrived at the other. The list that must always empty."
      where(status: "debited")
      order_by :status
    end
  end

  aggregate "ExternalTransfer" do
    given("transfer is sent") { status == "sent" }
    # Declared by ATMCard; see `CardPayment`.
    given("account is open", declared_by: ATMCard)
    given("customer is active", declared_by: ATMCard)
    # Unambiguous chapter-wide, so no `declared_by:` is needed.
    given("transfer is requested")
    description "A transfer sent beyond the bank, where a recall is an instruction and a return is the external network's outcome."

    reference_to Account
    # Same names ATMCard's projected fields use.
    projects :account_status,          from: :"account.status"
    projects :account_customer_status, from: :"account.customer_status"
    attribute :end_to_end, EndToEndReference

    identified_by :end_to_end
    attribute :amount,      ExternalAmount
    attribute :beneficiary, BeneficiaryName
    # The ledger's direction set, declared once on Account and named here rather than restated.
    attribute :direction,   MovementDirection, admits: "Account::LedgerDirection"

    value_object "EndToEndReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
    end

    # The type is local; the set of values belongs to Account, which `admits` names.
    value_object "MovementDirection" do
      attribute :value, String
    end

    value_object "ExternalAmount" do
      attribute :cents, Integer
      invariant("an external transfer amount is positive") { cents.positive? }
    end

    value_object "BeneficiaryName" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a beneficiary name is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "requested" do
      transition "SendTransfer" => "sent", from: "requested"
      transition "Recall" => "recalled", from: "sent"
      transition "Return" => "returned", from: "sent"
    end

    command "Request" do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Send money to an account outside the bank"

      attribute :end_to_end, EndToEndReference
      # `account` is a fresh command argument, so these read it directly.
      given("customer is active") { account.customer.status == "active" }
      given("account is open") { account.status == "open" }
      sets :account
      sets :amount
      sets :beneficiary
      sets :direction
      sets :end_to_end
      emits ExternalTransferRequested
    end

    # Each `from:` below matches a `transition` above.
    command "SendTransfer", from: "requested" do
      role "System"
      goal "Release the transfer to the external network"

      reference_to ExternalTransfer
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits ExternalTransferSent
    end

    command "Recall", from: "sent" do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Ask the external network to stop a transfer already sent"

      reference_to ExternalTransfer
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits ExternalTransferRecalled
    end

    command "Return", from: "sent" do
      role "System"
      goal "Record that the external network sent the money back"

      reference_to ExternalTransfer
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits ExternalTransferReturned
    end

    query "Sent" do
      description "Transfers already released to the external network, awaiting its outcome."
      where(status: "sent")
    end
  end

  aggregate "ScheduledPayment" do
    given("payment is failed") { status == "failed" }
    given("payment is scheduled") { status == "scheduled" }
    # Declared by ATMCard; see `CardPayment`.
    given("account is open", declared_by: ATMCard)
    given("customer is active", declared_by: ATMCard)
    description "An instruction held for a future date, which may execute once or be cancelled before it does."

    reference_to Account
    # Same names ATMCard's projected fields use.
    projects :account_status,          from: :"account.status"
    projects :account_customer_status, from: :"account.customer_status"
    attribute :amount,    ScheduledAmount
    attribute :instruction, InstructionReference

    identified_by :instruction

    attribute :recipient, PaymentRecipient
    attribute :due_on,    PaymentDueDate
    attribute :attempts,     RetryCount
    attribute :max_attempts, RetryLimit

    value_object "InstructionReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
    end

    value_object "ScheduledAmount" do
      attribute :cents, Integer
      invariant("a scheduled payment amount is positive") { cents.positive? }
    end

    value_object "PaymentRecipient" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a payment recipient is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "PaymentDueDate" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a payment due date is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "RetryCount" do
      attribute :value, Integer, default: 0
      invariant("a retry count is non-negative") { !value.negative? }
    end

    value_object "RetryLimit" do
      attribute :value, Integer, default: 3
      invariant("a retry limit is positive") { value.positive? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "scheduled" do
      transition "Execute" => "executed",  from: "scheduled"
      transition "Cancel"  => "cancelled", from: "scheduled"
      transition "Fail"    => "failed",    from: "scheduled"
      transition "Retry"   => "failed",    from: "failed"
      transition "Abandon" => "abandoned", from: "failed"
    end

    command "Schedule" do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Set up a payment to collect on a future date"

      attribute :instruction, InstructionReference
      # `account` is a fresh command argument, so these read it directly.
      given("customer is active") { account.customer.status == "active" }
      given("account is open") { account.status == "open" }
      sets :account
      sets :amount
      sets :recipient
      sets :due_on
      sets :instruction
      emits PaymentScheduled
    end

    # Each `from:` below matches a `transition` above.
    command "Execute", from: "scheduled" do
      role "System"
      goal "Collect a payment on its due date"

      reference_to ScheduledPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits ScheduledPaymentExecuted
    end

    command "Cancel", from: "scheduled" do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Call off a payment before its due date"

      reference_to ScheduledPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")
      emits ScheduledPaymentCancelled
    end

    command "Fail", from: "scheduled" do
      role "System"
      goal "Record that today's presentment could not be collected"

      reference_to ScheduledPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")

      emits ScheduledPaymentFailed
    end

    # Self-triggering on purpose: a re-presentment against an account still short of
    # funds fails again, and `RetryOnPaymentFailure` re-enters this command.
    # `max_attempts` is the bound, ordinarily inside the runtime's reaction-depth ceiling.
    #
    # Mutating, not creating: the reaction re-dispatches against the same record, and
    # a second creation would raise AlreadyExists.
    command "Retry", from: "failed" do
      role "System"
      goal "Re-present a failed payment, up to the limit the schedule names"

      reference_to ScheduledPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")

      given("a retry is still allowed") { attempts.value < max_attempts.value }

      sets :attempts, increment: { value: 1 }

      ensures("a retry never lowers the attempt count") { attempts.value == old.attempts.value + 1 }

      emits ScheduledPaymentFailed
    end

    command "Abandon", from: "failed" do
      role "Back office"
      goal "Give up on a payment that could not be collected after every retry"

      reference_to ScheduledPayment
      given("customer is active")
      given("account is open")

      given("every retry is exhausted") { attempts.value >= max_attempts.value }

      emits ScheduledPaymentAbandoned
    end

    query "Due" do
      description "Payments still scheduled, ordered by when they're due."
      where(status: "scheduled")
      order_by :due_on
    end

    policy "RetryOnPaymentFailure" do
      on      ScheduledPayment::ScheduledPaymentFailed
      trigger ScheduledPayment::Retry
    end
  end

  process_manager "Settlement" do
    # `reference` is the field Transfer.Request sets and `identified_by` derives the id from.
    correlates_by :"reference.value"
    starts_on Transfer::TransferRequested
    ends_on   Transfer::TransferSettled

    # Same `transition` vocabulary as `lifecycle`; states are implied by each `from:` and target.
    transition Transfer::TransferRequested => "requested", from: "requested" do
      # Debit never declared :destination; the credit leg reads it from the saga's
      # memory of the opening payload. `reference:` carries the correlation forward
      # (Account.Debit does not reference Transfer).
      #
      # `compensates` derives per-dispatch compensation from this declaration, so a
      # refused credit undoes the debit.
      dispatch Account::Debit, with: { number: :source, amount: :amount, narrative: { text: "transfer out" }, reference: :reference } do
        compensates Account::Credit, with: { number: :source, amount: :amount, narrative: { text: "transfer reversed" } }
      end
    end

    transition Account::AccountDebited => "awaiting_credit", from: "requested" do
      # `transfer:` is Transfer.Debited's own reference key, addressing the record; the
      # value is the correlation. No `compensates` on Credit: it is the leg most likely
      # to refuse, and a leg that never completed has nothing to undo.
      dispatch Transfer::Debited, with: { transfer: :reference }
      dispatch Account::Credit, with: { number: :destination, amount: :amount, narrative: { text: "transfer in" }, reference: :reference }
    end

    transition Account::AccountCredited => "awaiting_credit", from: "awaiting_credit" do
      dispatch Transfer::Credited, with: { transfer: :reference }
    end

    transition Transfer::TransferCredited => "settled", from: "awaiting_credit" do
      dispatch Transfer::Settle, with: { transfer: :reference }
    end

    # Hand-written, not `compensates`: it marks the transfer itself reversed on any refusal,
    # whichever leg declined.
    transition :refused => "reversed", from: "awaiting_credit" do
      dispatch Transfer::Reverse, with: { transfer: :reference }
    end
  end

  # Correlates on a different key over the external event stream, pointed at the network leg.
  # Keyed on the scalar `end_to_end.value`, not the value object, whose rendering is ambiguous.
  process_manager "ExternalSettlement" do
    correlates_by :"end_to_end.value"
    starts_on ExternalTransfer::ExternalTransferRequested
    ends_on   ExternalTransfer::ExternalTransferSent

    transition ExternalTransfer::ExternalTransferRequested => "requested", from: "requested" do
      dispatch ExternalTransfer::SendTransfer, with: { end_to_end: :end_to_end }
    end

    # The compensating leg: a refusal arms the return instead of leaving the request stranded.
    transition :refused => "returned", from: "requested" do
      dispatch ExternalTransfer::Return, with: { end_to_end: :end_to_end }
    end
  end

end
